classification_effect: Literature annotation and review recommendations. Released classification is unchanged by this file.

sources.title: Expression of Genes Encoding Multi-Transmembrane Proteins in Specific Primate Taste Cell Populations
sources.source_location: Human taste-bud results and Figure 10D; Methods: human tissue collection and PCR
sources.finding: CALHM3 RNA was measured by semi-quantitative PCR in laser-captured human circumvallate taste buds, with no detectable or reduced expression in surrounding lingual epithelium.
sources.limitations: Human data are RNA from a microdissected compartment. Cell-subtype in situ experiments elsewhere in this paper used macaques. This is not human protein detection or a therapeutic depletion experiment.
sources.retention_reason: Corrects the earlier mouse-only assessment of CALHM3 and supplies human normal-compartment counterevidence. It is not a CTA nomination.

memberships.scope: Exact human gene, normal circumvallate taste-bud RNA; Figure 10D
memberships.recommendation: Review hold: human normal taste-bud RNA plus the established mouse taste-channel function warrant a normal-compartment review before target clearance. Do not call this proven human protein or infer an injury outcome.
